svg.aria-label: Upper panel: a longitudinal section through a valley glacier from cirque to terminus, with the equilibrium line dividing accumulation from ablation, crevasses in the brittle upper ice, ductile flow beneath, a terminal moraine of unsorted till and a sorted outwash plain beyond it; insets compare a U-shaped glacial trough with the pre-glacial V-shaped valley and show a roche moutonnee. Lower panel: eccentricity, obliquity and precession curves over the last 500 thousand years plotted above a sawtooth ice-volume record whose terminations are abrupt and spaced about 100 thousand years apart.

g.text: (a) A valley glacier in longitudinal section
The ice flows down-valley whatever the terminus does: the snout advances or retreats as accumulation minus ablation.
(b) Orbital cycles and the ice-volume record, last 500 kyr
Terminations are abrupt and roughly 100 kyr apart — yet eccentricity is by far the weakest direct forcing.
